children: Federal Reserve officials were broadly positioned for further interest-rate increases in 2026, with most policymakers clustered around one additional hike while a smaller group favored more aggressive tightening, according to Deutsche Bank's reading of the September dot plot.

Deutsche Bank's identification of individual dots showed four regional Fed presidents, including three current voters, leaning toward 75 basis points of total hikes this year. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, and Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid were in that group, according to the bank's analysis.

Meanwhile, Fed Governors Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller were identified at the more dovish end of the 2026 distribution, projecting only one hike total for the year. The remaining 12 officials were estimated to be around the 4.125% median, anticipating one additional rate hike over the remainder of the year, according to Deutsche Bank's analysis.

The bank's chart showed four officials around 4.375%, while Bowman and Waller were near 3.875%. Most of the remaining officials were clustered around 4.125%, underscoring the concentration around the median policy path.

For 2027, the distribution was more divided. Deutsche Bank identified eight officials as favoring 75 basis points of total tightening through 2027, compared with six who appeared to favor 50 basis points. The bank also identified Waller, New York Fed President John Williams and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly as likely favoring some easing next year.
Another figure showed Bowman as the most dovish projection for 2027 at 3.1%, while several officials were clustered between roughly 4.1% and 4.4%.
The median long-run federal funds rate estimate also rose to 3.2% from 3.1%, while the mean increased to 3.3%, with both reaching post-pandemic highs, according to Deutsche Bank.

title: Fed officials cluster around further rate hikes in 2026
